assessment.overall_rationale: Left and right sets both decompose into a tip-cell/sprouting-angiogenesis module, a TGF-β-linked module, and (only on the left) an unrelated ion-channel/calcium module; the best cross-set matches are L1–R1 and L2–R3, with L2–R2 flagged as directionally opposed and L3 having no counterpart in the right set.

pair_scores.rationale: Both describe sprouting tip-cell identity in postnatal brain vasculature via Angpt2/Cxcr4/Cdc42ep3 downstream of Nrp1, but R1 is a narrower version lacking L1's Hopx/Gabarapl1/Tek content.
Shares Cxcr4, Hopx, Nrp1 and Tek regulator, but L1's core is general filopodial tip-cell identity while R2's core mechanism is Notch-driven CXCR4 coupling to arterial specification.
Only Angpt2/Nrp1 overlap; L1's CDC42-driven filopodia/sprouting mechanism is unrelated to R3's TGF-β-mediated vascular integrity/Angpt2-repression mechanism.
Shares Angpt2 and Nrp1 in a tip-cell identity context, but L2's defining mechanism is Tgfbr1/2-dependent D-tip specification whereas R1's is CDC42-driven filopodial guidance.

Both link Nrp1/TGF-β signaling to tip-versus-stalk fate, but L2 asserts CNS-specific TGF-β/Alk5 signaling promotes tip (D-tip) identity while R2 asserts Alk5/TGF-β shifts cells from tip toward stalk, a directional conflict.

Both center on Tgfbr1/Tgfbr2 as regulators whose loss decreases the program and on TGF-β repression of Angpt2, with R3 narrowing the output to vascular integrity/hemorrhage prevention versus L2's D-tip identity framing.
L3's ion-channel/calcium mechanosensing genes (Kcnj2, Cacna1c, Jph1) share no genes or mechanism with R1's tip-cell sprouting program.
No gene or mechanistic overlap between L3's membrane calcium/ion-channel signaling and R2's Notch-CXCR4-arterial specification axis.
L3's ion-channel mechanosensing module is biologically unrelated to R3's TGF-β/Angiopoietin-2 vascular integrity axis.
